s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of throat fullness, pain, and respiratory distress with localized inflammation and mass-like prominence at the base of the tongue
salient_findings: Rapidly progressive fullness in the throat
Dyspnea with local redness at the root of the tongue
Non-homogeneous mass-like prominence at the base of the tongue
key_facts: 3-day history of fever
Leukocytosis with a left shift
Elevated C-reactive protein
Normal thyroid-stimulating hormone, triiodothyronine, and thyroxine levels
Flexible laryngoscopy showed a non-homogeneous, mass-like prominence at the base of the tongue
Neck ultrasound failed to identify the thyroid gland in its normal pretracheal location
Contrast-enhanced CT scan demonstrated a non-homogeneous, contrast-enhancing area at the tongue base
Peripheral calcifications and adjacent nodular structures enhanced similarly to thyroid tissue

salient_findings: Rapidly progressive fullness in the throat
Dyspnea with local redness at the root of the tongue
Non-homogeneous mass-like prominence at the base of the tongue

shortlist.label: Lingual thyroid gland
shortlist.why_kept: Mass-like prominence at the base of the tongue and absence of thyroid gland in normal location

shortlist.label: Ectopic thyroid tissue
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of thyroid tissue at the base of the tongue and adjacent nodular structures enhancing similarly to thyroid tissue

shortlist.label: Thyroglossal duct cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Midline location and presence of calcifications, although less likely given the patient's age and clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Base of tongue abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of symptoms, fever, and leukocytosis, although the presence of ectopic thyroid tissue is more likely given the imaging findings

shortlist.label: Retropharyngeal abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Severe inflammation and respiratory distress, although the location of the mass-like prominence at the base of the tongue makes this diagnosis less likely

raw.rationale: The presence of a non-homogeneous, mass-like prominence at the base of the tongue, normal thyroid function tests, and the absence of a thyroid gland in its normal pretracheal location, along with imaging findings of a contrast-enhancing area at the tongue base with peripheral calcifications and nodular structures enhancing similarly to thyroid tissue, are consistent with a lingual thyroid gland.

rejected.label: Ectopic thyroid tissue
rejected.why: While ectopic thyroid tissue could explain some findings, the specific location and characteristics described are more suggestive of a lingual thyroid gland.

rejected.label: Thyroglossal duct cyst
rejected.why: Thyroglossal duct cysts typically present as a midline neck mass and may contain thyroid tissue, but the described location at the base of the tongue and the absence of a normal thyroid gland make this less likely.

rejected.label: Base of tongue abscess
rejected.why: The presence of fever and leukocytosis could suggest an abscess, but the imaging findings and the lack of other signs of infection, such as significant mucosal inflammation, make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Retropharyngeal abscess
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and imaging findings do not support a retropharyngeal abscess, which would typically present with more significant symptoms of infection and different imaging characteristics.
